findings.reason: The protected app source defines the required local ArrayReader but also exposes compareSub, length, and query methods belonging to unrelated reader problems, and its get method uses the campaign-forbidden generic parameter name index. The candidate supplies the minimal documented source-native model with only get(position), keeping the standalone contract self-contained and problem-specific.

The inert candidate removes unrelated reader machinery while preserving the Accepted exponential-bracketing and binary-search algorithm exactly. Its left, right, middle, value, position, and target names are conventional and precise, and the solve(reader, target) adapter retains the same behavior and asymptotic bounds.

Each expansion step discards a sorted prefix only after its rightmost accessor value is below target, then doubles the right boundary until a value at least as large as target or the out-of-range sentinel is reached. The resulting inclusive bracket contains every possible target position. Standard binary search preserves that possibility while halving the bracket, returning the unique matching position or -1 once the bracket is empty.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode problem 702, Python, and the native search(reader, target) interface. The candidate preserves strictly increasing hidden values, non-negative positional access through ArrayReader.get, the large out-of-range sentinel, a zero-based matching position, -1 absence, and the app-local list-to-reader adapter.

The protected app search method and immutable native source bound to verified submission 2065611037 use the same initial boundaries, doubling condition, boundary updates, midpoint calculation, comparisons, and absence result. The candidate changes only the local reader surface and accessor parameter name around that identical method; it remains inert and does not replace or alter the Accepted evidence.

The unchanged authored workloads grow hidden sorted arrays from 32 to 512 values with the target immediately above the maximum, forcing exponential bracketing to cross the end and binary search to establish absence. In a fresh real-test run, the exact candidate passed all eleven ordinary correctness cases and all three performance tiers with relative growth exponent -0.02 and a 0.99x largest runtime ratio; the protected source also passed with exponent -0.01 and a 0.99x ratio. A correct sequential scan passed every ordinary and benchmark output but failed only performance with relative growth exponent +0.52, distinguishing logarithmic accessor growth from linear traversal.

The candidate-targeted Approach identifies the minimal get-only app reader, derives exponential bracketing, explains sentinel termination and binary search, and proves no possible position is skipped. Its O(log n) time and O(1) auxiliary-space claims match the candidate and branch manifest.

The legacy document was replaced by a composition anchor and four modular Reference sections. The independent narrative preserves the interactive setting, unique strictly increasing secret values, unknown size, get-only access, zero-based indexing, exact out-of-bound sentinel, target result contract, required logarithmic runtime, both source examples with their explanations, and all three constraints. The contract explicitly distinguishes the source-native ArrayReader from the app-local list adapter.

Authenticated live Premium evidence verified the interactive description, reader behavior, logarithmic requirement, exactly two explained examples, all three constraints, and absence of visuals, notes, and follow-up sections. The modular Reference is bound to source content hash 8138dc579a74127436dd630bad22359d93ee592d9596d4dbbf22865ad5062d9c and every composed local section through source_fidelity.json; direct validation returns verified with no errors.

coverage: The authenticated Premium statement contains exactly two examples, each with an explanation of presence or absence. Their exact secret values, targets, and outputs appear first and in source order through the app-local reader adapter; the invented [1,2,4,8,16] sample was reclassified as a trial.

All ordinary correctness checks are visible samples or trials. The former hidden first-index, above-range sentinel, and singleton-miss behaviors were exposed or strengthened, leaving no correctness behavior concealed in cases.json.

Contract boundaries cover length one, values and targets at -10000 and 10000, the first and last legal positions, and targets below, above, and between stored values. The 10000-element maximum length was separately checked with first, middle, last, near-last-missing, and above-range targets without bloating an ordinary case; persisted benchmark tiers cover scaling behavior.

Material behavior covers the initial right boundary, repeated exponential doubling, expansion beyond the real end, sentinel termination, negative values, zero, singleton hit and miss, an interior gap, and both successful and absent searches.

Expected results were checked against independent bisect-based lookup across 26611 exhaustive strictly increasing array/target pairs, 500 deterministic random arrays, and five searches over a legal 10000-element maximum-length array. Protected app, inert candidate, and immutable native forms agreed throughout and on every authored case and benchmark.

All eleven ordinary cases are visible. The unchanged 32, 128, and 512-value workloads remain hidden and performance-only in benchmark.json, span 16x, and make the correct sequential-scan control fail only the scaling verdict.
